indian.headline: Indian markets closed down across the board; IT and auto weakness dragged indices lower.
indian.lead: Indian markets closed down across the board; IT and auto weakness dragged indices lower.
indian.brief: Sensex fell 1.17%, Nifty 50 dropped 1.07%, and Bank Nifty eased 0.78% in a broad market retreat.
why: IT sector slumped 1.9%, the sharpest decline among major segments, weighing on the Nifty and Sensex.
Auto stocks tumbled 1.5% while realty fell 1.4%, offsetting modest gains in metals (+1.4%) and energy (+0.1%).
Banking sector weakness of 0.8% and FMCG decline of 0.9% added pressure on defensive plays.
Rupee weakened to ₹92.98/$ (+0.80% USD/INR), raising import costs and pressuring exporters' margins.

drivers: IT sector sharp fall of 1.9% pulled heavyweight tech stocks lower on the index.
Auto decline of 1.5% and realty weakness of 1.4% offset metal gains, dragging the Sensex down.
IT sector's 1.9% drop hit the Nifty harder than the Sensex due to index composition.
Banking slide of 0.8% and FMCG fall of 0.9% limited any recovery from energy and metal pockets.
Banking sector declined 0.8%, reflecting broad caution in financials despite PSBs posting strong 18.8% credit growth.
News of regulatory scrutiny on the Tata Steel–APL Apollo deal added uncertainty to large-cap bank holdings.

indian.narrative:
Indian equities delivered a down day on 27 November 2026, with the Sensex sliding 1.17%, the Nifty 50 dropping 1.07%, and the Bank Nifty easing 0.78%. The selloff was broad-based, led by sharp declines in IT (down 1.9%), auto (down 1.5%), and realty (down 1.4%), while only metals managed a modest gain of 1.4%. Banking stocks fell 0.8% and FMCG declined 0.9%, signalling weakness even in defensive sectors. The rupee weakened to ₹92.98/$ on currency markets, adding to export headwinds.

Underlying the retreat were multiple crosscurrents. While macro tailwinds persist—J.P. Morgan forecasts Nifty reaching 29,000 in 2027 and PSBs posted record credit growth of 18.8% with net NPAs at a historic low of 0.33%—regulatory uncertainties surfaced around the Tata Steel–APL Apollo deal, with Sebi potentially investigating related-party transaction compliance. Meanwhile, gold rallied sharply to $3,704/oz (+4.77%), a typical haven move in risk-off markets, while Brent crude fell to $92.02/bbl (−2.74%), easing some inflation fears. The rupee's weakness, however, underscores currency volatility ahead of potential US tariff action on Indian goods, adding a near-term headwind to exporters.

us.headline: US markets ended mixed as tech weakness offset financial and energy gains amid tariff uncertainty.
us.lead: US markets ended mixed as tech weakness offset financial and energy gains amid tariff uncertainty.
us.brief: S&P 500 fell 0.25%, Nasdaq dropped 0.62%, but Dow rose 0.33% as investors rotated out of technology.
why: Tech sector sold off 0.8% as mega-cap AI stocks faced pressure, dragging growth-heavy Nasdaq lower despite modest S&P resilience.
Financials and Energy each gained 0.7%, showing investor shift to value and defensive sectors on tariff and economic concerns.
Gold surged 4.78% to $3,705/oz as risk aversion grew; oil fell 2.74% to $92.02/bbl on demand weakness and tariff fears.
Indian rupee weakened 0.80% to ₹92.98/$ as US tariff threats—up to 25% on Indian exports—created currency headwinds for traders.
us.narrative:
US equities delivered a mixed verdict on Wednesday as the market wrestled with competing forces. The Dow managed a small gain while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq both retreated, with technology stocks bearing the brunt of selling pressure after a prolonged rally in mega-cap AI names. Financials and Energy bucked the trend, each rising 0.7%, signaling a tactical rotation into cheaper valuations. Healthcare slipped 0.6%, adding to growth sector fatigue.

Commodity moves underscored investor caution. Gold jumped 4.78% to $3,705 per ounce—a classic flight-to-safety signal—while Brent crude fell 2.74% to $92.02 per barrel on demand concerns. The Indian rupee weakened sharply, losing 0.80% to ₹92.98 against the dollar, as traders digested the full scope of proposed US tariffs on Indian imports, which could reach 25% unless a trade deal cuts the rate to 17%. Deutsche Bank's call for a tech bottom and 25% S&P rally offered some optimism, yet rising default risk at SoftBank over stretched AI bets tempered enthusiasm. For Indian exporters and importers, the tariff proposal has injected fresh uncertainty into near-term planning.

tiles.sub: Safe-haven demand rises amid tariff and growth fears.

tiles.sub: Could drop to 17% if India and US strike trade deal.

tiles.sub: Tech weakness, tariff uncertainty, and AI debt concerns dominate.

us.watch: Watch whether Deutsche Bank's tech bottom call holds and if India-US trade talks accelerate tariff resolution.
